name: claude-plugin
description: Profile for Claude Code plugin repositories whose code is Python. Same Python toolchain as python-plugin-monorepo (Python 3.11+, uv, pytest, ruff, no deployable web server, no frontend) plus the architecture rules of plugin projects: what goes into scripts and what goes to the AI, Anthropic's skill limits, scripts run through uv run, hooks resolve paths through ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, generated files live next to their source. Adopt picks it when the repository has a .claude-plugin folder.

stack._comment_runtime: The claude-plugin key is the adopt matching signal (a .claude-plugin folder was found); adopt scores a profile by the dependency names it declares here.

folder_structure.plugins/: One Claude Code plugin per folder (each with .claude-plugin/, hooks/, skills/, agents/, scripts/, tests/, pyproject.toml)

architecture_rules.text: Checks, counts, comparisons and format rules go into scripts, tests or hooks; reading intent, judging wording and writing prose go to the AI. A SKILL.md names the decision and the script that makes it and does not restate the script's logic.
architecture_rules.why: Code checks the same way every time and prose that copies code drifts from it, while a script that guesses meaning is wrong reliably and looks trustworthy.

architecture_rules.text: Every skill keeps to the limits for name, description, SKILL.md body size and reference depth in shared/config/conventions.json (skill_authoring).
architecture_rules.why: A skill over Anthropic's limits is loaded badly or not at all, and the failure is silent.
architecture_rules.note: shared/scripts/tools/check_skill_authoring.py checks these limits but is a report today: no phase and no CI job runs it, so nothing stops a skill that breaks a limit. Wiring it in is outside this profile's first release.

architecture_rules.text: Python scripts are started with uv run, never with a bare python or pip.
architecture_rules.why: uv run gives the script the project's pinned interpreter and dependencies, so it behaves the same on every machine.
architecture_rules.note: No checker scans skills, hooks or scripts for a bare python call. The only mechanism is the narrower hook of the rule no-bare-python-stdin.

architecture_rules.text: Never run python - (an interpreter that reads its program from standard input) without a heredoc or pipe feeding it.
architecture_rules.why: Such a call waits on an input nobody answers and keeps a core busy for hours.
architecture_rules.note: The hook is registered by the shipwright-iterate plugin and denies the command only in Claude Code sessions where that plugin is active, and only for the Bash tool (the PowerShell tool is not guarded); it also refuses an empty heredoc feeding python -. It does not look at files in the repository. The mechanism path is relative to the Shipwright repository: a copy of this profile in a project's .shipwright/profiles/ must change this rule to prompt-only or drop the mechanism, or validate reports the path as missing.

architecture_rules.text: Hook commands and scripts reach plugin files through ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} (in double quotes), never through an absolute or working-directory-relative path.
architecture_rules.why: The plugin is installed into a cache folder that differs per machine and per version, and the quotes keep a path with spaces in one piece.
architecture_rules.note: No checker is wired into this profile. A test that checks the quoting of the placeholder exists only inside the Shipwright repository.

architecture_rules.text: A generated file lives next to the source it is generated from, not among hand-written files.
architecture_rules.why: Source and render are then read and reviewed together, and a stale render is easy to spot.
